title: Searching Ultra-Long Videos with Decision Models
title_zh: 用决策模型检索超长视频
abstract_en: Understanding ultra-long videos requires retrieving sparse, query-relevant evidence from extensive video histories. Existing similarity-based retrieval methods are efficient, but they encode the question and the video content independently and thus often miss evidence whose relevance requires reasoning over both. Generative large language models (LLMs) can perform such reasoning, but they typically generate text over multiple rounds of search, which makes each query slow and costly. In this work, we introduce DeLoVi (Decision Models for Long Video), a framework that leverages pretrained decision models to retrieve evidence from ultra-long videos. Like an LLM, a decision model reads the question together with the candidate evidence, so it can reason over both. Unlike an LLM, it directly outputs a relevance score without generating text, which makes it fast and inexpensive. We first present DeLoVi-S, a simple method that generates captions for short video clips and uses a decision model to rank those captions by their relevance to a question. A generative LLM then answers the question using the top-ranked captions. Despite its simplicity, DeLoVi-S achieves state-of-the-art performance on three ultra-long video understanding benchmarks, EgoLifeQA, EgoMemReason, and MM-Lifelong, and generalizes effectively to long-video understanding benchmarks, VideoMME-L and LVBench. However, DeLoVi-S scores every caption for every question, so its cost grows linearly with video length. To reduce this cost, we propose an automated policy evolution framework that iteratively refines the memory construction and retrieval policies around a fixed pretrained decision model. The resulting method, DeLoVi-E, maintains comparable performance while reducing input tokens by 34x on average compared with DeLoVi-S. It also runs over 3x faster than the best prior method on EgoLifeQA while achieving higher accuracy.
abstract_zh: 超长视频理解需要从大量视频内容中检索与问题相关的少量证据。基于相似度的方法分别编码问题和视频内容，容易漏掉需要结合两者推理才能识别的证据；生成式大语言模型（LLM）能进行联合推理，但多轮搜索中的文本生成增加了延迟和成本。本文提出 DeLoVi（Decision Models for Long Video），利用预训练决策模型联合读取问题与候选证据，直接输出相关性分数，无需在检索阶段生成文本。基础方法 DeLoVi-S 先为短视频片段生成文字描述，再对描述进行相关性排序，最后由生成式 LLM 根据排名靠前的描述回答问题。DeLoVi-S 在 EgoLifeQA、EgoMemReason 和 MM-Lifelong 上达到当时最佳表现，并有效泛化到 VideoMME-L 和 LVBench。但它需要为每个问题逐一评分，成本随视频长度线性增长。为此，DeLoVi-E 固定预训练决策模型，通过自动化策略演化迭代优化记忆构建和检索策略，在维持相近表现的同时，将平均输入 token 数降至 DeLoVi-S 的约 1/34；在 EgoLifeQA 上，其速度超过此前最佳方法的 3 倍，准确率也更高。
key_points_zh: 决策模型联合读取问题和候选证据，直接输出相关性分数，兼顾联合推理与检索效率。
DeLoVi-S 对短片段的文字描述逐一评分，再由生成式 LLM 基于高分描述作答；它在三个超长视频基准上达到当时最佳表现，但检索成本随视频长度线性增长。
DeLoVi-E 不更新决策模型，而是迭代优化记忆构建与检索策略；在表现相近的情况下，平均输入 token 数仅为 DeLoVi-S 的约 1/34。
在 EgoLifeQA 上，DeLoVi-E 比此前最佳方法准确率更高，运行速度超过其 3 倍。
